evidence.note: Early on identified both deliverables and their numeric thresholds; established the two targets as distinct goals, though without an explicit written plan.
Enacted a real pipeline: convert format -> run SANA aligner -> build independent eval/scorer script for S3/NC -> optimize. Stages are clearly separable.
Repeatedly treated the numeric bars (0.32; 0.55/0.30) as concrete milestones, checking current scores against them per deliverable.
Built reusable greedy and SA optimizers plus a shared scorer applied to both pairs — shared infrastructure factored from per-instance tuning.
Ran both deliverables concurrently in background rather than deliberately sequencing the single-bar DM-HS vs the dual-bar y2kr-SC; caused CPU contention.
Reactively re-decomposed when DM-HS plateaued at ~0.26 (tried graphlets, L-GRAAL), showing some adaptation but no formal iteration checkpoints.

reasoning: The agent clearly went beyond anchor 5: distinct stages (parse/convert, align, score, optimize, write) with the two numeric thresholds serving as explicit per-deliverable milestones, and it factored shared infrastructure (scorer, reusable greedy/SA optimizers) from per-instance tuning — a trait of anchor 8. However it falls short of a full 8 because there was no structured upfront plan and no deliberate easier-first sequencing (the two pairs ran concurrently), and short of 10 because the optimization loop lacked formalized intermediate checkpoints; adaptation was reactive flailing rather than principled re-decomposition. This places it at a 6.
